Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 105, verse 1–5:

.. We will review it briefly, the explanation of the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ [al-Fil 1] to the end of the surah, because it is the surah we have already covered earlier.

Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ He addresses the Prophet (ﷺ), or He addresses everyone to whom the address may properly be directed. On the first view, the address to the Prophet (ﷺ) is an address to him and to the Ummah, because his Ummah follows him. On the second view, the address is general, to him and to his Ummah from the outset. In either case, Allah, the Exalted, establishes what He, glorified and exalted, did to the companions of the elephant.

The companions of the elephant were the people of Yemen who came to demolish the Ka'bah with a great elephant sent to them by the king of Abyssinia. The reason for this was that the king of Yemen wanted to turn people away from pilgrimage to the Ka'bah, the House of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So he built a house resembling the Ka'bah and called people to make pilgrimage to it, in order to divert them from the pilgrimage to the House of Allah. The Arabs became angry at this, and a man from them went to this house that the king of Yemen had made in place of the Ka'bah, defecated in it, and smeared its walls with filth. The king of Yemen became extremely angry and informed the king of Abyssinia of this, so he sent this great elephant to him. It is said that there were six other elephants with it to assist it. This man, meaning the king of Yemen, came with his troops to demolish the Ka'bah, as he supposed, but Allah, glorified and exalted, is the Guardian of His House. When they reached a place called al-Mughammas, the elephant stopped, balked, and refused to head toward the Ka'bah. Its driver beat it, but it refused. When they turned it toward Yemen, it went off running, but when they turned it toward Makkah, it stopped. This was one of the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then they remained until Allah sent against them ﴿birds in flocks (3), striking them with stones of baked clay﴾ [al-Fil 3, 4].

The scholars said: ﴿birds in flocks﴾ means groups dispersed, each bird carrying in its beak a hard stone of sijjil, which is baked clay, because it is harder. This stone was not large; rather it was small, striking one of them along with his head and coming out from his rear, and we seek refuge in Allah.

﴿And He made them like eaten straw﴾ [al-Fil 5], meaning: like crops eaten by animals and trampled underfoot until they were crushed.

This is the summary of this great surah, in which Allah, glorified and exalted, explains what He did to the companions of the elephant, and that their plot turned back against them. Likewise, whoever intends evil against the truth, Allah, the Exalted, will turn his plot back against his own neck.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, protected the Ka'bah from this elephant, although [it is reported that] "at the end of time a man from Abyssinia will be empowered over it, who will demolish it stone by stone until it is leveled with the ground"[[Al-Bukhari (1595) narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "As if I see him, a black man with bowed legs, pulling it out stone by stone."]]. The story of the companions of the elephant was a prelude to the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), in which the House is glorified. As for the end of time, when the people of the House insult it, intend to violate it through wrongdoing, and do not recognize its sanctity, then Allah will empower over it whoever demolishes it so that nothing remains on the face of the earth. For this reason, the people of Makkah in particular must guard against sins, transgressions, and major wrongs, lest they disrespect the Ka'bah and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, humiliates them. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to protect our religion and His Sacred House from the plotting of every plotter; indeed, He is capable of all things.
